question: Your team asks Claude Code to add a caching layer to a payment-status service. The developer assigned to the task has never built a cache before. The developer worries that important design decisions will be missed. Which actions apply the interview pattern to surface these considerations before implementation?

options.text: Ask Claude Code to build the full cache first, and then ask it to list the questions that the implementation raised.
options.reason: The guide places the interview before implementing, so questions raised after the build come too late to shape the design.

options.text: Ask Claude Code to question the developer about cache invalidation strategies, such as when entries must expire after a status update, before writing any code.
options.reason: In the interview pattern, Claude asks questions that surface considerations such as cache invalidation before implementing in an unfamiliar domain.

options.text: Have Claude Code ask the developer how the service must behave when the cache backend fails, and settle those answers before implementation starts.
options.reason: The guide names failure modes as a design consideration that the interview pattern surfaces before implementation.

options.text: Have the developer write a long prose specification alone and tell Claude Code to implement it without asking any clarifying questions.
options.reason: The interview pattern has Claude ask questions because the developer may not anticipate every consideration, so blocking questions defeats it.

options.text: Let Claude Code implement the cache immediately with direct execution, and then fix the design problems that appear during code review.
options.reason: The interview pattern surfaces considerations before implementing, so it does not wait for problems to appear in finished code.
